_doc: DERIVED. The historical sheets published as SELECTABLE overlays, per the owner's ruling of 2026-08-06: an era is its own switchable layer, never merged into present-day geometry, so the present can be enriched from it later without either having overwritten the other. `toleranceKm` is per LAYER and the three layers of one sheet differ by more than ten times - a boundary drawn from the physiographic tier would be wrong by a county. `creator: null` is an open credit gap, not a licence. `bounds` is measured from the geometry as [west, south, east, north] and is what a camera flies to when the reader asks to see that era's ground. Rebuild with tools/publish-era-layers.py.

eras.title: Political map of NEW CALIFORNIA REPUBLIC and the NEW WEST, in the year 2253
eras.region: California, Nevada, Baja, the Pacific north-west
eras.creator: u/Polakp
eras.licence: none printed - STILL BLOCKS PUBLICATION of anything derived. A name is not a licence. But the author is now identified and reachable, so the question moves from unanswerable to ASKABLE, and asking is the owner's step.
eras.registration: equidistant conic fitted to its printed graticule, 0.78 km median against Natural Earth's coastline

layers.label: Administrative divisions
layers.note: The sheet's own inset, registered separately and less precisely than the main map.

layers.label: Territorial control
layers.note: Who holds the ground, as the sheet draws it.

layers.label: Physical features
layers.note: Named ranges, valleys and basins. These are LABEL ANCHORS: where the name sits.

eras.title: Fallout Mexico — the Mexican Wastes
eras.creator: u/omega-lf
eras.licence: none stated by the author - still gated
eras.registration: EQUIRECTANGULAR with a standard parallel near 24N, rotated 1.26 degrees. NOT plate carree and - against the expectation carried in from the Savannah sheet - NOT Mercator either. Mercator does beat plate carree by 28%, but only because its sec(phi) ratio happens to be near the ratio the sheet wants; freeing x and y scales on a plain equirectangular beats Mercator, and the two become indistinguishable. The test that separates them: fit on one latitude half and score on the other. Equirectangular generalises across latitude and Mercator does not, by up to 2.2x, in both directions.

layers.label: Polity and tribe names
layers.note: Where a NAME sits, never where the thing is, and never where its border runs. An anchor says the faction is here; a sheet in this residual band cannot say more.

layers.label: Settlements
layers.note: Point sites the sheet prints a marker for. Positions are the marker centroid, found mechanically; only the names were read by eye. Features with positional: false carry NO usable position - the sheet draws that ground wrong - and the reason is on the feature. toleranceKm below is the worst among the features that DO have a position.

layers.label: Spheres of influence
layers.note: Reach rather than sovereignty: ground a power's writ runs over without that ground being a state of its own. FOUR sheets reach for this independently - West Coast Civilizations and NCR & Legion 2281 draw it as soft gradients around hard control, north-america-2290's author states 'lighter colors surrounding national borders implies influence in a given area', and Savannah 2313's author calls his internal divisions 'trading spheres of influence'. Savannah's are the first extracted, and they are the inward-facing case: one state's own trade divisions, which are NOT provinces and NOT polities. Never read a feature here as a sovereign border.
